name: create-survey-solicitation
narrative: Maya has designed her matched study. But to measure her own program credibly, the survey has to be run by someone independent. So she needs to recruit a survey firm — to visit the households and collect the outcomes. Rather than start a separate process, she turns the finished study into a call for a firm on the Connect network, with the wards, coverage, and scope already attached. Maya's finished Round 6 study sits in her portfolio, flagged ready to solicit — and right on the card is the way to turn that plan into a call for a survey firm, no separate tool. Maya builds the call. The title and coverage carry over from her study, so a firm sees exactly the wards she sampled. She adds a description and the scope of work, sets the type and the status, and leaves it publicly listed across the whole Connect network — or pointed at organizations she already knows work here. Then the deadline and the expected start and end dates, the estimated scale, and her contact. Finally she writes an application question every firm must answer. Then, instead of hand-writing a scoring rubric, she clicks Generate with AI — and the platform drafts the evaluation criteria, weighted, straight from her scope and her questions. Each criterion carries its own weight and a scoring guide, so two reviewers reading the same response should land in the same place. She reads them, keeps them, and publishes the call — the rubric is fixed before a single firm has seen it. The applicant sees the coverage on offer. The firm names itself, adds an email, confirms the wards it can staff, then reads the criteria it will be judged against beside each question — and drafts its answer. Before submitting, the firm runs its draft through the AI Application Coach — which reads it against those same published criteria and suggests where to strengthen it: press for verifiable evidence, not unbacked claims. It is the same rubric the reviewer will use, so the firm is not guessing at what counts. The firm picks the coverage it can staff, and submits. Back in her workspace, Maya opens the responses and sees Sahel Field Research tied to the exact coverage she designed. Maya sets the budget the winning firm will be paid, then awards Sahel Field Research — the screen records the decision and notifies the organization. Standing up the live opportunity is the next step, not yet built.

firm.intro: Sahel Field Research is an independent northern-Nigeria household-survey firm looking for survey work it can staff; it answers public solicitations with the coverage its enumerators can commit to. It names itself in the response form's "Your organization" block, so the owner reviews and awards a named firm rather than the individual account that submitted the application.
firm.name: Sahel Field Research

maya.intro: Maya designed the Round 6 two-arm Attakar-versus-Gura study for her Vitamin-A programme and now needs to recruit the independent firm that will run the household survey on it.

features.description: The program workspace (portfolio) renders a "Create solicitation" link on every plan card and study-group card, to /solicitations/create/?source_program_id=<pid>&source_group_id=<gid>
features.verify: Playwright: on /microplans/program/10008/, assert the R6 — Attakar × Gura study-group card reads as finished (the "Attakar × Gura" arm-pair title, a Reviewed status badge, the "Finished study — ready to recruit a survey firm" marker, "2 wards") and renders a primary "Create solicitation" anchor whose href contains source_group_id=4492

scenes.narrative: Maya's finished Round 6 study sits in her portfolio, flagged ready to solicit — and right on the card is the way to turn that plan into a call for a survey firm, no separate tool.
scenes.title: Maya turns her finished study into a call for a firm

features.description: The create form renders a Coverage-areas panel populated from the snapshotted plans (source_plan_ids=[4494]), drawing the wards as a real map — Attakar (intervention, green) and Gura (comparison, blue) polygons fit to bounds
features.verify: Playwright: on the create form with source_group_id=4492, assert a "#sol-coverage-map" element renders a mapbox canvas and that the page text includes "Attakar" and "Gura"

features.description: Submitting the create form with status=active mints a new type=solicitation record on program 10008 and redirects to /solicitations/<new-id>/responses/ ("Review and manage responses"), from which the new solicitation_id is captured on camera
features.verify: Playwright: after clicking "Create Solicitation" with status set to Active, assert the URL matches /solicitations/(\d+)/responses/?created=1 and the page reads "Solicitation published — organizations can now apply"

features.description: The Generate-with-AI button POSTs scope+questions to /solicitations/api/generate-criteria/ and renders AI-drafted criteria in the criteria builder
features.verify: Playwright: click Generate with AI and assert an input[x-model=criterion.name] appears within 50s

features.description: The public response form draws the coverage as an interactive map — clicking a ward boundary toggles its whole parent plan, synced two-way with the "Which areas can you cover?" checklist; submit is blocked until at least one area is selected
features.verify: Playwright: on /solicitations/${solicitation_id}/respond/, assert a "#sol-respond-map" mapbox canvas renders the Attakar/Gura wards and a "#sol-plan-checklist" checkbox for the R6 plan; ticking the R6 area enables Submit (≥1 required to submit)

features.description: The response form carries a "Your organization" identity block (firm name + contact email) so a firm answering a public call names itself; the entered firm name is stored as the response's org_name / submitted_by_name and shown to the owner on the responses list and award screen, instead of the individual account that submitted the form
features.verify: Playwright: on /solicitations/${solicitation_id}/respond/, assert "#id_firm_name" and "#id_firm_email" inputs render; after filling firm name "Sahel Field Research" and submitting, the responses list row reads "Sahel Field Research" (not the operator account email)

features.description: Submitting the response redirects to the solicitation's public detail page (/solicitations/${solicitation_id}/?submitted=1) which shows a "Response submitted" confirmation receipt for the coverage the firm committed to
features.verify: Playwright: after clicking "Submit Response", assert the URL is /solicitations/${solicitation_id}/ and the page text includes "Response submitted"

features.description: The coach POSTs the draft answers to ai:ai_stream (application_coach agent) and renders coaching suggestions in #coach-content
features.verify: Playwright: click #coach-btn and assert the button text flips to Get Feedback Again within 55s

features.description: The responses list shows each response's selected_plan_names resolved against the solicitation snapshot, and renders an Award action linking to /solicitations/response/<response-id>/award/
features.verify: Playwright: on /solicitations/${solicitation_id}/responses/, assert the submitted response row shows "R6 — Attakar" as its selected coverage area and an "Award" link whose href contains response/<id>/award

features.description: The award screen summarizes the applying firm (Sahel Field Research, the name it entered on its application) with its selected coverage, and on award records the decision and confirms the organization was notified ("Awarded to Sahel Field Research — the organization has been notified"); it does NOT, on award, provision a Connect opportunity or push the plan's work areas into one — that downstream step is deferred (G1)
features.verify: Playwright: on /solicitations/response/${response_id}/award/, after award assert a confirmation reading "Awarded to Sahel Field Research" and "has been notified", plus a "Next step — not yet built" panel; grep: no create_opportunity/WorkArea-provision call in connect_labs/solicitations/
